name: Illinois
summary_text: “Most Protective” tier in the July 2026 assessment: regional non-discrimination covering gender identity and shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state actions; no state-specific negative finding beyond the shared federal layer (passport/API policy, priced into the national score). No country-unique finding beyond insurance-coverage details a visitor never encounters. Clearly above the national score 0.36.

sources.title: Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map: July 2026
sources.claim_summary: Erin Reed's anti-trans national legal-risk assessment map (July 2026 update, via Stonewall News): grades every US state's legislative risk for transgender adults; Idaho entered the top 'Do Not Travel' tier (felony bathroom ban, up to 5 years; the map's fourth such state) and South Carolina rose to 'Worst Laws Passed'; catalogues the nationwide federal rollback (passport and legal-document barriers, funding withdrawals, Pride-crosswalk erasure) and several countries' travel advisories for trans travellers. Lists Illinois among 'Most Protective States (CA, CO, CT, HI, IL, MA, MD, MN, NJ, NM, NY, OR, RI, VT, WA)' — states that have gone above and beyond in safeguarding transgender people's rights.

sources.title: Transgender Healthcare "Shield" Laws - Movement Advancement Project
sources.claim_summary: Movement Advancement Project equality map of transgender healthcare 'shield' laws (data as of Sept 2026): 16 states plus DC have shield laws and two more protect access by executive order, shielding trans people, their families and providers — including people who travel from states where care is banned — against out-of-state civil or criminal action. Illinois is among the shield-law states (the state-level roster renders interactively; the dossier cites this page).
